answer: Give new identities shadow seats: for their first twenty epochs, their grades are recorded and checked against final outcomes but carry zero weight. An operator who spins up a hundred clones to sink a rival's atlas of harbor depths and canyon currents gets no swing on that verdict. Each clone must first match honest outcomes for months before its vote counts, so a sudden flood of fresh accounts changes nothing, and keeping a farm alive that long costs real, graded work per head.
